targetWords.definition: To accomplish something means to finish it.
targetWords.example: He accomplished his goal of running ten miles.

targetWords.definition: To approve of something means you like it or are happy about it.
targetWords.example: Her co-workers approved her new plan.

targetWords.definition: Approximate means to be close to an exact amount, number or time.
targetWords.example: My approximate height is two meters. barrier [baeriar] n.

targetWords.definition: -* The Great Wall was a barrier between China and its enemies.
targetWords.example: The Great Wall was a barrier between China and its enemies.

targetWords.definition: To detect something means to notice or find something.
targetWords.example: ■The boy ran to the kitchen when he detected the smell of cookies. duty [d/'u:ti] n.

targetWords.definition: -* It is parents' duty to take care of their children.
targetWords.example: It is parents' duty to take care of their children.

targetWords.definition: When something is elementary, it is the first or most simple thing.
targetWords.example: Children go to elementary school before high school. failure [feiljar] n.

targetWords.definition: -» My cooking ended in failure because I burned the food.
targetWords.example: My cooking ended in failure because I burned the food.

targetWords.definition: When something is gradual, it happens slowly.
targetWords.example: Children learn to read at a gradual pace. They do not learn right away.

targetWords.definition: An immigrant is a person who moves to a different country.
targetWords.example: My parents were immigrants. They came from Poland.

targetWords.definition: To insert something means to put it in something else.
targetWords.example: The mailman inserted the letter into the mailbox.

targetWords.definition: r
targetWords.example: A microwave oven cooks food in an instant. poverty [pavarti] n.

targetWords.definition: Poverty is the state of being poor.
targetWords.example: Poverty is a problem in many countries around the world.

targetWords.definition: To pretend means to make believe something is real.
targetWords.example: • The boy liked to pretend he was a king.

targetWords.definition: A person's rank is their place in an order of people.
targetWords.example: The man got to the rank of captain in the navy.

targetWords.definition: Recognition is getting praise from other people.
targetWords.example: The hero got recognition for his brave deed.

targetWords.definition: To refrigerate something means to make it cold.
targetWords.example: Grocery stores refrigerate fruit to make it last long.

targetWords.definition: Rent is the money people pay to someone to live in a certain place.
targetWords.example: To live in this house, I have to pay rent at the start of each month.

targetWords.definition: To retire is to leave a job, usually because of old age.
targetWords.example: ■My father is sixty-five years old. He is about to retire from work.

targetWords.definition: A statistic is a number that tells a fact about something.
targetWords.example: The statistics showed that we did just as well this year as last year. ^23

story.title: Albert Einstein
story.passage:
My name is Albert Einstein. Many people know about the great things I've

accomplished. But I had many barriers before I became famous.

I was born in Germany. When I was in elementary school, I already knew

about math and statistics. When I was a boy, I pretended to be a great scientist.

I loved school, but my life at home was hard. My father lost his job, so my family

lived in poverty. We could not pay the rent in Germany. We became immigrants

and went to Italy. I finished high school and went to college in Switzerland.

After college, I began writing about science. I did not reach success in an

instant, though. At first, other scientists did not approve of my work. They

thought I was a failure. Rising to the rank of an admired scientist was a gradual

process. Soon, people started to notice that I was right. At last, I began to get

some recognition.

I showed how to find the approximate size of very big things, like stars. I also

detected and explained the movement of very small things, like atoms. And

for fun, I made a machine that could

refrigerate food by inserting

heat. I never retired. It

was my duty to keep

working. I overcame

many hard times,

and I will be

remembered

for my

important

works.

questions.question: Why did Einstein's family become immigrants?

options.text: They were unhappy about new developments in math and statistics.
They couldn't pay their rent in Germany and had to leave.
His parents didn't want him to stay in school.
They wanted Einstein to go to college in Switzerland.

questions.question: Why was Einstein's rise in the ranks of scientists gradual?

options.text: Einstein did not write down his ideas.
Einstein's ideas could not be proven.
Other scientists already knew about his ideas.
Other scientists didn't approve of his ideas at first.

he refrigerated food by inserting heat as a power source

he detected the movement of atoms
